error.signature: AI tells a foreigner in Mexico that a passport and residence permit alone are enough to enroll in public healthcare or complete official registrations
error.regex: (curp.*mexico|clave unica de registro de poblacion|mexico.*imss.*enroll|need curp mexico|mexico.*registration.*passport only)

verdict.summary: CURP (Clave Única de Registro de Población) is Mexico's population-registry number and is a prerequisite for many transactions, including enrolling in IMSS's public health insurance. Per the official SEGOB procedure, foreigners are only eligible for a CURP once INM grants them residente temporal or residente permanente status - a tourist on an FMM visitor permit cannot get one no matter how long they stay, and a passport plus residence card does not substitute for it.

dead_ends.action: Tell a foreigner staying in Mexico on a tourist FMM permit that they can get a CURP by visiting a RENAPO/DDV office with just their passport
dead_ends.why_fails: The official gob.mx procedure 'Asignación de CURP' restricts issuance to foreigners who have been granted residente temporal or residente permanente status by INM; the CURP is generated automatically, tied to the Número Único de Extranjero, once that residency status is granted - it is not a separate request an FMM tourist can make.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That CURP is available to any foreigner physically present in Mexico regardless of visa/permit status.

dead_ends.action: Assume enrolling in IMSS's Seguro de Salud para la Familia (voluntary public health insurance) only requires a passport and proof of address
dead_ends.why_fails: IMSS's own online enrollment procedure (trámite imss02014) requires a CURP and an NSS (Social Security Number) for every family member before the form can be submitted; without a CURP - which itself requires resident status - the online route is closed, and in-person enrollment still depends on the same underlying registry number.
dead_ends.condition: Enrolling in Seguro de Salud para la Familia (Modality 33)

workarounds.action: Apply for residente temporal or residente permanente status with INM (via a Mexican consulate abroad, or in-country for qualifying cases) before expecting to obtain a CURP
workarounds.how: Once INM issues the resident card with its Número Único de Extranjero, RENAPO's system generates the CURP automatically - it is not a request made separately at a RENAPO counter.
workarounds.condition: Intending to stay long-term or access CURP-gated services

workarounds.action: For a short/tourist stay, plan around CURP-gated services instead of expecting to obtain one - use private healthcare or travel insurance rather than IMSS enrollment, and cash or a foreign card where a CURP-linked account would otherwise be required
workarounds.condition: Tourist or short-term visitor without residency status
